note: S17.2 (the CLAMP as ONE order-independent solve, the determinism proof). Two anchored chains re-converging on the shrinking side: v@600 full-span (id:1) + h@500 spanning x in [600,1000] (id:2) splits the RIGHT region into a top-right cell (1:1:0, bound to a min w=350 window) and a bottom-right cell (1:1:1, min w=300), each currently w=400. Drag v@600 by delta=+200 (coord pushes RIGHT, shrinking both right cells — a large over-shrink). For delta>0 the clamp filters A::incident to the frame_min_x==600 (far) side = BOTH right cells; room = min over the SET of (size - cell_min) = min(400-350, 400-300) = min(50,100) = 50, so cd = +50 and L lands at coord 650 (the tighter w=350 floor binds). The harness computes the clamp TWO ways (the bag's segment order forward + reversed, and move_line over both) and asserts byte-equal cd (cd_byte_eq) AND byte-equal final segment SET (arr_segs_seteq): A::incident dedups by cell so a re-converging shared cell contributes its (size-min) term ONCE — min is commutative/associative/idempotent → the realized geometry is independent of evaluation order. A greedy per-chain cascade would over-clamp (subtract chain-A's allocation then re-clamp B against the residual); the min-over-set never does.
